business_problem: British Sugar needed to preserve expert knowledge, improve production and supply-chain decisions, and reduce downtime and cost by moving from intuition and siloed processes to data-driven operations.
solution_summary: British Sugar partnered with IBM Research and IBM Consulting to build an AI-driven operating model around a supply-chain digital twin and predictive-maintenance capabilities. The first stage created a digital twin of the early supply-chain lifecycle, powered by Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service on Microsoft Azure, so the company could simulate scenarios without disrupting production. In parallel, British Sugar built a predictive-maintenance MVP using IoT sensors, machine learning and data analytics to identify equipment-failure patterns and reduce downtime. The company then integrated these models into control systems and decision workflows so experts could summarize thousands of data points quickly, improve supplier visibility and make real-time adjustments across production, water usage and purification processes. The resulting architecture combines simulation, operational telemetry and AI-assisted knowledge capture to drive faster decisions and preserve technical know-how.

solution_components.role: Implemented the business transformation framework spanning digital twin, predictive maintenance and knowledge workflows.

data_flow: Operational and supplier data flow from IoT sensors and business systems into a digital twin and predictive models, where simulations and analytics are used to adjust production, maintenance and supply-chain decisions in near real time.
business_outcome: British Sugar improved decision speed, reduced downtime and raw-material costs and created a scalable knowledge and simulation framework that helps new staff ramp faster and operations adapt more quickly.
metrics: 20% reduction in the duration spent manually understanding data and information
20% reduction in the average time to resolve production issues
10% reduction in costs of raw material for purification processes
architecture_clues: Digital twin currently focused on the “make” part of the supply chain
Predictive-maintenance MVP uses IoT sensors, machine learning and data analytics
AI models are integrated directly into data control systems
evidence_quotes: Working closely with IBM Research® and the IBM Consulting® AI and Analytics practice, they deployed a business transformation framework to address its challenges.
The first step was to develop a digital twin of the early stages of its supply chain lifecycle, powered by Microsoft Azure OpenAI service and hosted on the Microsoft Azure Cloud Platform.
As a result of this proof of concept, the company reduced failures and downtime from rotating equipment.
